questions.question: What does the traction motor in an EV actually do to make the car move?

answers.a: It turns mechanical energy from the wheels into electrical energy for the battery.
answers.b: It converts the electrical energy stored in the battery pack into mechanical energy.
answers.c: It changes chemical energy directly into mechanical energy to turn the wheels.
answers.d: It generates thermal energy to help power the vehicle’s auxiliary systems.

explanations.a: This is regenerative braking, not the main way the car moves forward.
explanations.b: Correct. As per THEORY.pdf, the battery gives power to the traction motor, which changes electrical energy into mechanical energy to make the vehicle move.
explanations.c: Normal gas cars do this, but EVs use stored electrical energy instead.
explanations.d: The motor is built to create movement from electricity, not to make heat for other things.

questions.question: If my EV motor runs at a power level of P = 2000 W for a total driving time of t = 1.5 hours, how much energy (E) is consumed in Watt-hours (Wh)?

explanations.a: This happens if you divide power by time instead of multiplying them.
explanations.b: This would only be right if the car drove for exactly 1 hour.
explanations.c: Correct. Based on the formula E = P x t in THEORY.pdf, you multiply 2000 W by 1.5 hours to get 3000 Wh.
explanations.d: This looks like a math mistake with the decimal point.

questions.question: Why does driving aggressively (like slamming on the gas pedal) lower your driving range?

answers.a: It requires a large amount of power within a short period of time, leading to faster energy depletion.
answers.b: It causes the traction motor to completely shut off to protect the battery.
answers.c: It decreases the overall driving time, which automatically wastes battery power.
answers.d: It changes the battery's chemical composition, making it unable to hold a charge.

explanations.a: Correct. THEORY.pdf explains that rapid acceleration takes a lot of power really fast, which drains the battery quicker.
explanations.b: Stepping on the gas makes the motor draw more power, it doesn't shut it off.
explanations.c: Even if you reach your destination faster, the huge power draw still ruins your efficiency.
explanations.d: Aggressive driving makes the battery drain faster, but it doesn't change its actual internal chemistry.

questions.question: What does 'State of Charge' (SOC) mean when checking your EV's battery status?

answers.a: The total distance the vehicle can travel before you have to plug it in.
answers.b: The rate at which power is being drained from the battery pack every second.
answers.c: The amount of energy remaining in the battery at any given time, shown as a percentage.
answers.d: The maximum capacity of a brand-new battery pack.

explanations.a: This is the driving range, not the battery state itself.
explanations.b: This describes power consumption or how fast energy is being used.
explanations.c: Correct. THEORY.pdf states that State of Charge (SOC) is just the energy left in the battery at any time, written as a percentage.
explanations.d: This is the total capacity of the battery pack, which doesn't constantly change while driving.

questions.question: How does getting stuck in a heavy stop-and-go traffic jam affect an electric car's battery consumption?

answers.a: It makes energy use more efficient because you are moving much slower.
answers.b: It has no effect because the AI system automatically cuts off power demand.
answers.c: It allows the vehicle to maintain a stable speed, which saves battery life.
answers.d: It causes repeated stopping and starting, which increases motor power demand and battery consumption.

explanations.a: Moving slow doesn't help because the constant stopping and starting ruins efficiency.
explanations.b: The AI only tracks your habits and gives tips, it can't change how traffic physically affects the car.
explanations.c: You can only keep a stable speed in light traffic, not a jam.
explanations.d: Correct. According to THEORY.pdf, heavy traffic forces you to constantly stop and start, which makes the motor work harder and uses more battery.
